introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.description: Samuel UI is an original Design System study created to explore how visual decisions can be organized, documented and transformed into reusable components. The project brings foundations, tokens, components and patterns into the same structure, showing both the design reasoning and the decisions involved in implementation.
introduction.whatBody: Samuel UI began as a practical exercise to demonstrate my approach to building interfaces and visual systems. Here, each choice moves through different layers of the system, from foundations such as color, typography and spacing to tokens, states, properties, accessibility and component implementation. More than creating an extensive library, the goal is to show how I think about the relationship between visual structure, documentation and front end.
introduction.whyBody: The project uses five components as a base to explore different Design System challenges: Button, Input, Select, Modal and Card. The quantity is intentional. The focus is on the depth of each component, exploring composition, variants, states, behavior, accessibility and documentation. With this reduced scope, I can show the decisions behind the system more clearly without turning the project into a complete library.

installation.title: Installation
installation.description: Samuel UI is developed as a pnpm workspace. The package is not published to npm yet — clone the repository to use it locally.

designPrinciples.title: Design Principles
designPrinciples.description: The rules that shape every component decision in Samuel UI.

principles.title: Composition over configuration
principles.body: Compound components (Modal.Root, Modal.Trigger, Modal.Content…) instead of one giant component with dozens of boolean props.

principles.title: Tokens, not values
principles.body: No component reads a raw hex or pixel value. Everything resolves through semantic CSS variables so themes stay consistent by construction.

principles.title: Accessible by default
principles.body: Keyboard interaction, focus management and ARIA are part of the component, not a follow-up task. Radix primitives handle it where the behavior is complex (Select, Modal).

principles.title: Documentation is a first-class product
principles.body: The docs site and Storybook consume the same real components and the same AI context files — there is exactly one source of truth.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: Primitive scales feed semantic tokens, which are the only colors components are allowed to reference. Values shown resolve for the active theme.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Three families, one job each: Inter Tight for headings, Inter for body copy, JetBrains Mono for labels, code and anything technical.

samples.heading: Design and code
samples.body: A design system for people who ship.

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.description: A 4px-based scale used consistently for padding, gaps and layout rhythm across the whole system.

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: A small, deliberate set of radii — sharp enough to feel technical, soft enough to feel considered.

shadows.title: Shadows
shadows.description: Elevation levels. Dark mode uses ambient black shadows; light mode softens them so nothing looks muddy on a bright surface.

levels.sm: Subtle lift — hovered rows, small controls.
levels.lg: Modals and anything floating above the page.
levels.focus: Focus ring — brand-colored, replaces default outline.

button.title: Button
button.description: Triggers an action or event, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.

a11y.native: Renders a native button element, so keyboard and screen reader support come for free.
a11y.loading: loading sets aria-busy and disables the button, but never hides its accessible name.
a11y.focus: Focus is always visible through --shadow-focus and is never removed without a replacement.

api.size: Controls height, padding and font size.
api.loading: Shows a spinner and disables the button.

input.title: Input
input.description: A labeled text field with helper and error messages, built as a compound component that shares state through context.

a11y.label: Label and control are linked automatically through a generated id and htmlFor pair.
a11y.describedby: aria-describedby points to the helper or error text, and aria-invalid follows the invalid prop.
a11y.error: Error text has role="alert" so assistive tech announces it when it appears.

api.invalid: Marks every child as invalid (border, aria-invalid, error styling).
api.disabled: Disables Input.Control unless overridden directly on it.

select.title: Select
select.description: An accessible dropdown selection, wrapping Radix UI Select for keyboard navigation and focus management.

a11y.keyboard: Keyboard navigation (arrow keys, typeahead, Home and End), focus management and ARIA roles all come from Radix UI Select, so none of it is reimplemented here.
a11y.value: The trigger exposes the current value to screen readers via Select.Value.
a11y.disabledItem: Disabled items stay visible and are still announced, they just can't be selected.

modal.title: Modal
modal.description: An accessible dialog for blocking interactions that require user attention, built on Radix UI Dialog.

examples.confirmDescription: This will make your changes visible to everyone.

a11y.radix: Focus trap, Escape-to-close, scroll lock and overlay click-to-close all come from Radix UI Dialog.
a11y.title: Modal.Title is required, since Radix uses it as the dialog's accessible name.
a11y.focusReturn: Focus returns to the trigger element when the modal closes.

api.open: Controlled or uncontrolled open state (on Modal.Root).
api.hideCloseButton: Hides the top-right close icon on Modal.Content.

card.title: Card
card.description: A flexible surface container, recomposed for different situations instead of turning into a one-off "ProjectCard".
card.projectCardBody: Tokens, components and documentation shipped together.
card.profileCardBody: Design Engineer, focused on Design Systems and UI Engineering.
card.docsCardBody: Install, import tokens, render your first component.

a11y.heading: Card.Title renders an h3 heading, so keep the heading order around it sane.
a11y.interactive: There's no implicit interactivity. Wrap the whole card in a link or button yourself if the entire surface needs to be clickable.

api.className: Merged with the default classes on Card.Root. No other props are exposed, composition covers the rest.
